title: 'When's my turn?' Men cheered as woman was raped at Chicago fraternity party
content: Mia Lara, a 21-year-old student at a nearby university, told The New York Times that she attended the party with the woman who reported the assault and another friend after seeing it advertised on the fraternity’s Instagram account. It was the first fraternity party any of the three had attended.

title: ‘Where did you sell gold chains?’ New videos give big twist to Sharma murder case
content: After Shraddha Dubey's confrontational videos with Shiva Sharma went viral, new footage emerged showing her demanding the return of jewelry she claims was stolen. The situation escalated following Shiva's fatal fall from an apartment building on October 9, prompting police to search for Shraddha and her associates while offering rewards for information. Investigators have yet to verify the authenticity of the videos or the surrounding events.

title: OpenAI’s office spy case shows why Google, Anthropic and others should be worried
content: OpenAI's office spy case is a warning for the whole AI industry. An engineer allegedly hid a Rs 1,200 recording device behind a TV in an executive conference room before OpenAI used its own AI models to trace him. According to WSJ, employees at Google and Anthropic have also received similar spy warnings, as trillion-dollar valuations make AI companies far bigger targets for corporate espionage.

title: Sara Blakely put $5,000 into Spanx; 21 years later, it was valued at $1.2bn
content: Sara Blakely founded Spanx in 2000 with $5,000 in savings while working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson. Despite having no formal business training or outside investment, she built the company into a global womenswear brand. In 2021, Blackstone acquired a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation, with Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joining as investors.

title: Rs 1 cr+ salaries: Amid layoff, which IT jobs are getting huge salary premiums?
content: Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior. Which roles are in demand? What are the average salary levels for special capability sets and which roles are under pressure? The premium concentrates in four families, AI, Data, Cloud and Cybersecurity, and peaks where capability depth meets governance and scale.

title: Sports ministry reviews Asian Games performance; questions injuries, lacklustre show
content: India's disappointing medal tally at the 2026 Asian Games prompted scrutiny from the Sports Ministry, with calls for National Sports Federations (NSFs) to take greater responsibility. In a meeting on Thursday, emphasis was placed on developing a pipeline of athletes rather than relying on a few stars. Preparations for future events, including the 2028 Olympics and 2030 Commonwealth Games, were also discussed, highlighting the need for better support systems.

title: Missile heading towards Medina destroyed, says Saudi Arabia; Houthis deny attack
content: A missile targeting Saudi Arabia's Medina region was intercepted by the Saudi-led coalition according to their spokesperson. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree refuted this claim, stating no operations were conducted towards Saudi territories. The ongoing conflict has resulted in a series of airstrikes from both the Houthis and coalition forces. Recent incidents include the destruction of a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh by the coalition.

title: Glasgow dig uncovers wall torn down by residents in 1823 riverside access fight
content: Archaeologists in Glasgow have uncovered remains of a 12-foot wall built by a wealthy distiller to block public access to the River Clyde in the 1820s. Residents tore down the wall in 1823, leading to arrests and a six-year legal battle. The excavation also revealed a rare 1791 trade token bearing the city's motto, "Let Glasgow Flourish".

title: Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law for $270,000; court rejects right to stay
content: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.

title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg leaving Meta CEO flattered
content: Alexandr Wang recently shared his admiration for Mark Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional leadership and decision-making skills. Wang pointed out Zuckerberg's readiness to make bold strategic changes grounded in deep convictions, a trait that sets him apart in the tech world. Initially taken aback, Wang grew to respect Zuckerberg's approach. In a lighthearted exchange, Zuckerberg acknowledged the compliment, showcasing Meta's focus on decisive executive actions.

title: Tyler Perry turned 330-acre former Army base into major Atlanta film studio
content: In 2015, Tyler Perry acquired the former Fort McPherson Army base in Atlanta for $30 million, and transformed it into a major production hub featuring 12 sound stages. This initiative not only aims to create new jobs but also emphasizes the importance of preserving historical structures while meeting the evolving demands of the film industry. Perry’s vision includes nurturing local talent to foster growth in South Atlanta's creative landscape.

title: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal launches political outfit, to contest 2027 UP polls
content: Divya Mittal has launched a political outfit named Jan Niti Bharat aimed at impacting Uttar Pradesh's 2027 elections. She emphasized three pledges focusing on citizen participation, needs-based decisions, and transparency in public works. Mittal expressed her desire to put people at the center of policymaking and engage directly with citizens. Her initiative reflects a response to overwhelming support from the public after she indicated her political ambitions.

title: Serena Williams reveals why she couldn't fully give up chicken for a vegan diet
content: Inspired by her sister Venus, Serena Williams delved into vegan eating, motivated by a desire for healthier choices. Although she found plant-based meals appealing, her love for chicken and tacos posed a challenge. During the 2013 French Open, her positive experience with a vegan diet reignited her interest, showcasing her commitment to embracing healthier eating habits while navigating the complexities of dietary change.

title: Nick Sirianni faces criticism: Why is Michael Vick asking Eagles fans for patience?
content: Michael Vick has come forward to back Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni amidst mounting frustration from fans following a tough defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Vick emphasizes the need for patience with both the coaching staff and quarterback Jalen Hurts, as rising tensions come from the offensive difficulties contributing to a three-game losing streak.

title: Meet Holden Bierman, 19, who turned $500 loan into six-figure beachwear business
content: At just 12 years old, Holden Bierman founded Coastal Cool during the pandemic with a modest $500 loan. Originally selling casual apparel, he shifted focus to creating eco-friendly swimwear made from recycled materials. By partnering with Tidey Ocean, Bierman supports ocean plastic removal with every sale. While managing his business, he sacrifices typical high school experiences but aims to expand retail and study business at university.

For one man, Gyanesh Kumar,” Dipke said, referring to the Chief Election Commissioner.

title: Wyoming ranch held by one family for four generations lists for $24.5 million
content: The Quarter Circle Lazy B Ranch, spanning 1,542 acres in Wyoming, is now on the market for $24.5 million. This family-owned property has been in the Wallop family since 1889 and hosted notable guests like Queen Elizabeth II. The ranch features a luxury lodge, multiple homes, and retains its panoramic mountain views and tranquility. Accessible to the town of Sheridan, the ranch offers both privacy and outdoor recreation opportunities.

title: Andaman woman turns 5 birds into poultry unit earning Rs 1.91 lakh monthly
content: Rajeshwari, hailing from Wandoor village, initiated her journey with just five birds and has since cultivated a thriving poultry venture. Armed with training from ICAR-CIARI, she honed vital skills in poultry management and currently produces approximately 2,000 chicks monthly. Her profitable business not only sells meat and eggs but also serves as an inspiration for others in rural settings, motivating them towards self-employment.

title: Can a strand from natural wig found in crime scene lead to trouble for donor
content: Donated hair found at crime scenes poses challenges in linking donors to criminal activities due to scientific constraints. DNA testing from cut hair is typically ineffective, making traceability difficult. Investigators must establish a clear connection between the donor and the crime, which is often complex. Police may contact donors for information, but that does not imply guilt or accusation.

Other high-end spirits, including premium vodka and gin, have also experienced considerable price increases. The excise department is enforcing compliance with the new maximum retail prices, warning sellers that violations may lead to severe penalties.

title: From viral fame to violent deaths: 3 Punjab influencers murdered in 16 months

Mad Sandhu was shot dead, Kanchan Kumari was found strangled, and Manjeet Kaur succumbed to severe burn injuries. Investigations into their deaths did not establish clear motives linking their online content to these killings. The incidents have sparked discussions about the safety of public figures and threats they face.

content: Russian diesel exports have started reaching global markets following an agreement with US President Donald Trump. The Kremlin stated that these supplies could help stabilize oil markets, but they will not suffice. Reports indicate that Russian shipments of diesel resumed from the Baltic port of Primorsk recently. Ukraine's leadership and various European officials have strongly criticized this deal amid ongoing conflict.

title: Trouble beneath the waves: India’s submarine fleet is ageing and replacements are years away
content: The Indian Navy is currently operating an ageing submarine fleet with plans for expansion by 2030. The current fleet consists of 16 conventional submarines and three strategic submarines. Significant delays have been experienced in the procurement of new vessels, including the planned P-75I program. The navy aims to enhance its capabilities with domestic and foreign collaborations for nuclear-powered attack submarines.

title: Hawaii’s Hāʻena State Park reopens 39 days after hurricane closure
content: Hā‘ena State Park on Kaua‘i reopened on October 15 after being closed due to Hurricane Lowell. Visitors can now access specific hiking trails and Kē‘ē Beach, but restrictions remain. Overnight camping is still prohibited, while hiking beyond two miles along the Kalalau Trail is not allowed. Other state parks on Kaua‘i remain closed or have limited access due to extensive storm damage.

title: Tampa Theatre reopens after seven-month, $24.5m restoration in its 100th year
content: Tampa Theatre has successfully wrapped up an extensive restoration initiative that commenced earlier this year. This project focused on revamping treasured decorations and upgrading essential infrastructure for future enhancements. A newly added education wing will support community-driven programs and classes, bolstering its cultural significance. Historical artifacts have been recovered and restored, ensuring the protection of its legacy.

title: She bought Rs 13.5 lakh shares, sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh; gets tax notice

The company subsequently issued bonus shares in a 1:1 ratio, which increased her holding to 1.2 lakh shares. The woman sold the shares between August 31 and December 24, 2012, and got around Rs 77,47,600.

title: Commission orders Rs 15 lakh refund after Force Motors vehicle developed engine defect
content: A Karnataka consumer commission found an inherent manufacturing defect in a bus purchased by a driver. The vehicle faced serious engine problems within months of its purchase. The commission examined evidence and ruled in favor of the complainant. Force Motors and the dealer were directed to replace the bus or refund the purchase price with interest. Compensation for mental agony and litigation costs were also awarded to the complainant.

title: 'Concern over anti-India hate in US': MEA demands probe into Hindu temple attack plot

It called for a comprehensive investigation came following the arrest of Alexandros Paporakis in Illinois, accused of plotting a mass shooting driven at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. Authorities uncovered alarming evidence tied to extremist views at his residence, leading the MEA to demand justice and advocate for community safety measures.

Gavaskar also highlighted the need for India's batters to take more responsibility during their chase.

title: India’s Sept exports rise 23% as trade deficit narrows; shipments to US rise 11%
content: India's merchandise exports rose to $44.40 billion in September 2026, marking a significant year-on-year increase. Overall exports, including services, also grew to an estimated $80.75 billion during this period. Despite rising imports to $94.05 billion, the merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion. Negotiations for a trade agreement with the US are reportedly progressing towards an early conclusion.
